qt: to the Commission Georgios Kyrtsos (Renew) Subject:
Economic war against investigative media outlet Documento and the systematic restriction of press freedom in Greece

In its annual Index, Reporters Without Borders, an institutional partner of the European Parliament, ranks Greece last among the 27 EU Member States for press freedom. In at 105th place (out of 180 countries), it performed worse than countries in the Western Balkans that are hoping to join the EU. A case which illustrates the methods being used to restrict media freedom is the economic war being waged against the opposition weekly Documento, which has a long-standing tradition of investigative reporting and big scoops to its name such as those concerning the Novartis and wiretapping scandals. The newspaper is being systematically deprived of State and private advertising as well as facing SLAPP-style lawsuits and, more recently, tax controls which have resulted in Documento being fined hundreds of thousands of euros, posing a threat to its financial viability. All this plays a part in limiting press freedom and is a breach of EU rules on rule of law. In view of this: 1.
What initiatives could the Commission take to help put an end to the economic war being waged in Greece against media that are critical of the government?
What is it doing to try to help strengthen media freedom and rule of law in Greece?

(8 May 2024) Freedom of expression and safety of journalists are a priority for the Commission. Member States should ensure an enabling environment for journalists and the media operating in their territory. The Commission regularly monitors media freedom and pluralism in Member States, including in the context of the Rule of Law Report. Regarding Greece, the Commission refers to the 2023 Rule of Law Report (1), which highlights progress in establishing safeguards to improve the working conditions and physical safety of journalists, acknowledging the creation of a task force for the protection and empowerment of journalists as important step, while calling for adoption of non-legislative safeguards and start of the legislative process in relation to the protection of journalists. To strengthen media freedom and pluralism, as well as the protection of journalists, the Commission put forward several EU initiatives, including the recommendation on the safety of journalists (2), the anti-strategic lawsuits against public participation Directive (3) and the European Media Freedom Act (EMFA) (4). The latter will strengthen the market and editorial freedom of media companies in the EU and protect them from unjustified, disproportionate and discriminatory national measures, thus enhancing free movement of services and protecting the pluralism of the European media landscape. It includes safeguards for journalists to perform their job freely and safely (5), as well as rules against state advertising being allocated based on discriminatory criteria and procedures (6). The Commission continues to closely follow developments on the above areas in all Member States, notably in the context of the upcoming 2024 Rule of Law report.

https://commission.europa.eu/publications/2023-rule-law-report-communication-and-country-chapters_en https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/recommendation-protection-safety-and-empowerment-journalists https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52022PC0177 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_23_6635 The EMFA requires that national measures taken by a Member State that are liable to affect media pluralism or the editorial independence of media service providers operating in the internal market shall be duly justified and proportionate. Such measures shall be reasoned, transparent, objective and nondiscriminatory. The EMFA requires public authorities to base the allocation of state advertising to providers or media services and online platforms on transparent, objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory criteria and to publish information about their advertising expenditures.
